prompt: A rectangle has corners at $(1, 2), (1, 6), (5, 2), (5, 6)$. What is its **perimeter**?
hint: Perimeter is the distance around the shape. You need the lengths of the sides, and the coordinates of the corners tell you those lengths.

hints.title: 🔁 Another angle
hints.text: Sketch the four corners on a grid. Then count the unit steps along the bottom side and along one upright side.
Perimeter is the distance around the shape. You need the lengths of the sides, and the coordinates of the corners tell you those lengths.
The $x$-values go from $1$ to $5$, so the width is $|5 - 1| = 4$. The $y$-values go from $2$ to $6$, so the height is $|6 - 2| = 4$. Add up all four sides.
Perimeter $= 2(4 + 4) = 16$, so the distance around the rectangle is $16$ units.

explanation: The corners use only the $x$-values $1$ and $5$, so the horizontal sides have length $|5 - 1| = 4$.
The corners use only the $y$-values $2$ and $6$, so the vertical sides have length $|6 - 2| = 4$.
Perimeter is the sum of all four sides, which is two widths plus two heights: $2(4) + 2(4)$.
That gives $8 + 8 = 16$, so the perimeter is $16$ units.
